regenerate: npm run rule-cases, in the website repository. Do not edit by hand.
conventions: A runner calls the rule named by a suite's "operation" with each case's "input" and compares the result with "expected". See rule-cases/README.md in the website repository.
Numbers are IEEE 754 doubles and must match exactly, with no tolerance.
Rounding sends ties towards positive infinity: 4.25 to the half is 4.5, and -0.25 to the half is 0. Half-even rounding is wrong.
A missing object key means the value is absent. Key order means nothing; array order does.
A null grade means the Fach has no Teilfach with grades, so it has no grade at all. The website computes NaN here.
A grade of 0 means a Subject with no grades or only zero weights.
Promotion leaves out null and every grade at or below 0. A Fach average leaves out only Teilfächer with no grades, so a Teilfach with grades that ends at 0 still counts.

types.Grade: { id, value, weight, label?, semester?: "Herbstsemester" | "Frühlingssemester", date? }. On entry, value is 1 to 6 and weight is above 0, both rounded to two decimals; date is an ISO date.
types.Subject: { id, name, grades: Grade[], kind?: "spf" | "ef", oralGrade? }. Told apart by its grades key.
types.CombinedSubject: A Fach of Teilfächer: { id, name, subjects: Subject[], unassignedGrades?: Grade[] }. Told apart by its subjects key.
types.GymProfile: { thirdLanguage?, arts?, spf?, ef? }: names for the first two, ids from subjectChoices for the others.
types.StudentData: { dataVersion?: the data format, a missing value means 1, studentInfo?: { name, division: "FMS" | "Gymnasium" }, currentYear: the selected year, 1 to 4, year3Direction?: a Berufsfeld id, gymProfile?: GymProfile, years: { "1" to "4": { subjects: (Subject | CombinedSubject)[] } } }
types.PromotionStatus: { isPassing, hasGrades, criteria: { failures: { passed, count, max }, average?: { passed, value, min }, deficit?: { passed, value, max }, compensation?: { passed, surplus, deficit, factor } } }. FMS has average and deficit, the Gymnasium has compensation.
types.PromotionVerdict: "noGrades" | "passing" | "notPassing". What the student sees. Decide from this, because isPassing can be true with no grades.

suites.description: Rounds to the nearest 0.5, used for every Fach and Teilfach grade. Ties go towards positive infinity.
Rounds to two decimals, used for the average, deficit and surplus. Grade values and weights are rounded this way on entry. Works on the double as stored, so 1.005 lands below its tie.
The rounded grade of a Subject or CombinedSubject. The oral adjustment is added before rounding; a Fach averages its rounded Teilfach grades.
